content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired (PD#98765) for service=private-vpc-routing. Severity=critical. Symptom: multi-account peering flaps observed between acct-A and acct-B causing control-plane RPC timeouts and intermittent on-prem agent disconnects. Affected customer: AcmeCorp (private deployment, two peering sessions). First seen: 2026-03-14T03:57:02Z. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-98765 :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: acked on PD and Slack. I'm on it — taking lead for next 30m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to oncall-alex. Escalation policy: SRE -> Neteng -> Eng-Ops.

oncall-alex: Quick triage notes: saw a spike of control-plane 504/503s correlating with BGP flaps on the peering sessions. Agent heartbeats drop during flaps, then most come back.

sre-maya: adding context — we saw route withdraws from the peering fabric at 03:56:58Z, then re-advertise. KV cache errors in logs around the same time. Pulling agent logs now.

network-ryan: jumping in. Which VPC/VPN attachments? Need ASN and session IDs.

oncall-alex: acct-A: vpc-0a1b2c (peer-session id ps-73), acct-B: vpc-7f8e9d (ps-82). Both peering sessions are across our transit gateway peering fabric.

eng-ops-june: tagged the runbook: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/private-vpc-peering-failures — steps 1-4 helpful. Recommending quick mitigation: enable route dampening and failover to backup peering in acct-B if available.

sre-maya: extracting agent logs. Sample error from agent on node acme-agent-12: ```
ERROR 2026-03-14T03:56:59Z agent_conn: heartbeat lost: EOF
WARN 2026-03-14T03:57:01Z controlplane: rpc timeout (3000ms)
```

network-ryan: I see BGP UPDATE storms on the peering link — looks like an unstable intermediate router in partner ASN causing route oscillation. Working with infra to identify the exact fabric node.

oncall-alex: @customer-success-ash flagged AcmeCorp. Ash, pls open a high-priority support channel and let customer know we're investigating; customer-facing summary: "Intermittent connectivity causing API 503s for private inference in acme-prod. Engineers are investigating and applying mitigations."

customer-success-ash: On it. Sending initial message to the customer's technical contact and their network team. Will post reply when they confirm receipt. :phone:

eng-ops-june: Proposed mitigation steps I'm going to try now (short maintenance window): 1) withdraw the problematic peering route at fabric edge for 60s to allow stable route selection; 2) force agents to reconnect to backup peering path; 3) if that doesn't hold, push a temporary ACL to avoid churn from a flaky neighbor. Will coordinate with network-ryan.

network-ryan: Agreed. I'll identify the flaky next-hop and isolate it. If we can pin the transit path to alternate node, that should stop the oscillation.

oncall-alex: Please paste exact commands you plan so I can approve quickly.

eng-ops-june: Commands (fabric control plane): ```bash
# soft-withdraw route for ps-73
fabricctl peer withdraw --peer ps-73 --duration 60s --reason "temp-isolate-flap"
# force reconnect agents via config push
redwood-agentctl restart --selector "cluster:acme-prod" --grace 5
```

oncall-alex: Approved. Proceed, and monitor agent heartbeats and 5xx rate.

incident-bot: Action executed: fabricctl withdraw completed for ps-73. Restart jobs queued (approx 25 agents).

sre-maya: Metrics update: agent heartbeat failure rate dropped from 18% to 3% within 45s of the withdraw. 5xx API error rate for AcmeCorp decreased from 12/min to 1/min.

customer-success-ash: AcmeCorp replied: "We see reduced errors — thanks. Will keep monitoring on our side."

network-ryan: Fabric node isolated. Confirmed BGP sessions stable for last 5 minutes. No further update storms observed.

oncall-alex: Handing off to SRE for sustainment and postmortem. @sre-maya, you'll take the incident for the follow-up and RCA. I'm standing by for any escalation.

sre-maya: Taking handoff. I'll collect datasets (BGP updates, agent logs, control-plane RPC traces) and schedule a 60-min RCA doc.

eng-ops-june: Leaving a short-term mitigation note in runbook: "If multi-account peering flaps observed, isolate flaky fabric node and failover agents to backup peering. Contact network oncall to remediate upstream device."

oncall-alex: Final customer impact assessment (preliminary): Affected tenant: AcmeCorp (private). Window: 03:56:58Z - 03:58:40Z (~1m40s of severe flapping; intermittent degradation for additional ~3m). Impact: Increased API 503/504, transient agent disconnects. Estimated % of requests impacted during peak: ~4-7% across Acme's private endpoints. No data loss.

customer-success-ash: Customer ops thanked the team and requested a follow-up timeline. Ash to own comms for SOC update.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD#98765 automatically resolved (closed by oncall-alex).

sre-maya: I'll compile the post-incident summary and share the RCA in #postmortems within 12h. Attached checklist: collect BGP dump, fabric node inventory, agent reconnect traces, and customer-perceived error samples.

oncall-alex: Thanks team. React with :thumbsup: if no further action required from current oncall.

network-ryan: :thumbsup:
eng-ops-june: :thumbsup:
sre-maya: :thumbsup:
customer-success-ash: :thumbsup:
